title: Inspiration4 crew serum cytokines, Eve HD71 + HDCVD9 (OSD-575)

source.name: OSD-575: SpaceX Inspiration4 Blood Serum Metabolic Panel and Immune/Cardiac Cytokine Arrays (Comprehensive Metabolic Panel and Multiplex)
source.license: not stated in the OSDR API response; the files are publicly released (OSDR file records 'restricted': false). Check the OSDR study page before reuse.
source.citation: NASA Open Science Data Repository (OSDR). OSD-575: SpaceX Inspiration4 Blood Serum Metabolic Panel and Immune/Cardiac Cytokine Arrays (Comprehensive Metabolic Panel and Multiplex). Study version 3, submitted 2022-12-05, publicly released 2024-05-14. https://osdr.nasa.gov/bio/repo/data/studies/OSD-575 (no dataset DOI is stated in the OSDR metadata). Investigators listed by OSDR: Christopher Mason (principal investigator); Eliah Overbey (co-investigator); Kirill Grigorev (formal analysis role); Theodore Nelson (formal analysis role). Publications listed by OSDR: The Space Omics and Medical Atlas (SOMA) and international astronaut biobank (doi:10.1038/s41586-024-07639-y); Collection of Biospecimens from the Inspiration4 Mission Establishes the Standards for the Space Omics and Medical Atlas (SOMA) (doi:10.1038/s41467-024-48806-z); CAMbank: SST Field Processing v1 (doi:10.17504/protocols.io.81wgbxxo1lpk/v1).

caveats: Inspiration4 was a ~3-day civilian low-Earth-orbit flight (OSDR metadata: mission 2021-09-16 to 2021-09-18) with n=4 crew. These files contain NO in-flight samples: only pre-flight L-92/L-44/L-3 and post-flight R+1/R+45/R+82/R+194 (the OSDR study description says 'The crew collected biospecimen samples before, during, and after flight', but no in-flight sample is in these files). These files provide a real post-flight recovery shape only (no reference ranges exist in these files); they are NOT a model of a long-duration exploration mission and must not be presented as one.

within_own_range is an OBSERVATION (value inside the reference range the laboratory printed for that same sample, bounds inclusive; one-sided ranges compare one bound), not an alert, not a diagnosis and not a NASA threshold. NASA publishes no numeric in-flight alert threshold for these analytes.
Timepoint dates are nominal and derived (label offset from the OSDR mission start for L-, from the mission end for R+); actual collection timestamps are not in these files.

Research multiplex immunoassays (Eve Technologies): the files carry NO clinical reference range, so ranges and within_own_range are null. Compare a crewmember only with their own pre-flight values; absolute cut-offs would be invented.
Values are the 'Concentration' column of the lab-submitted files; the 'Percent' column is not included because its normalisation basis is not documented in the files fetched.
Immune and cardiovascular status are OBSERVED and cited, not modelled as a LANDFALL case.
OSD-575 also holds an Alamar NULISA-seq 200-plex serum panel; it is not ingested here (relative NPQ units, size budget).

Exact repeats: the same multi-digit value recurs in several different crew/timepoint samples of one analyte (rule: >= 4 significant digits in >= 3 samples). The files carry no out-of-range or censoring flag, so these are reproduced as published, but they are not plausible as independent measurements (possibly values substituted at an assay limit) and should not be read as precise levels or used as a baseline. Listed per analyte in exact_repeats: IFN-α2 120.88 pg/mL x4 (C001 R+82, C003 L-92, C003 L-3, C003 R+45); IL-28A 15.56 pg/mL x5 (C002 R+82, C004 L-92, C004 L-3, C004 R+1, C004 R+45); Haptoglobin 17907000 ng/mL x7 (C002 R+82, C003 L-92, C004 L-92, C004 L-3, C004 R+1, C004 R+45, C004 R+194)
